Bonbons Sirop (Haitian Lime Syrup Candies)

Served at: Fete de Papa Zaka - Feast of the Farmer Loa

Makes about 30-40 small candiesPrep 15 minCook 25-30 min

These traditional Haitian syrup candies, known as Bonbons Sirop, are a simple yet beloved sweet often prepared for celebrations like Fete de Papa Zaka. Honoring Papa Zaka, the Lwa of agriculture, this feast is a time to give thanks for the harvest, and these sweet treats symbolize the bounty and simple joys of the land. Their bright lime flavor offers a refreshing taste of Haitian culinary tradition, perfect for offerings or sharing.

Ingredients

  • 2 cups (400 g) granulated sugar
  • 1/2 cup (120 ml) water
  • 2 tablespoons fresh lime juice
  • 1/4 teaspoon lime zest (optional)
  • Pinch of salt
  • Optional: 1-2 drops green or pink food coloring
  • Butter or oil for greasing

Method

  1. Lightly grease an 8x8 inch (20x20 cm) baking dish or a heatproof, non-stick surface with butter or oil.
  2. In a heavy-bottomed saucepan, combine the sugar, water, lime juice, lime zest (if using), and salt.
  3. Stir over medium heat until the sugar dissolves completely. Avoid stirring once the sugar has dissolved to prevent crystallization.
  4. Increase heat to medium-high and bring the syrup to a boil. Insert a candy thermometer, ensuring it doesn't touch the bottom of the pan.
  5. Boil the syrup without stirring until it reaches 250°F (121°C) for a chewier candy, or 280°F (138°C) for a firmer, slightly brittle candy. This will take approximately 15-20 minutes.
  6. Once the desired temperature is reached, remove the saucepan from the heat. If using food coloring, stir it in quickly.
  7. Carefully pour the hot syrup into the prepared baking dish. Do not scrape the bottom of the pan.
  8. Allow the candy to cool undisturbed for about 20-30 minutes, or until it is firm enough to cut but still slightly pliable.
  9. Using a buttered knife or pizza cutter, score the candy into small squares or rectangles while it's still warm.
  10. Let the candy cool completely at room temperature for at least 1 hour, or until fully hardened.
  11. Once completely cool and hard, break or cut along the scored lines to separate the individual bonbons.

Tips

  • For a ginger flavor, add 1 teaspoon of grated fresh ginger to the syrup at the beginning and strain it out before pouring.
  • Store bonbons in an airtight container at room temperature, separated by parchment paper, for up to 2 weeks.
  • Be extremely careful when working with hot sugar, as it can cause severe burns. Have all your tools ready before you start.
